text:
The Athletic declared this month that Zach Benson "has arrived as a star." The underlying numbers agree. The goal column doesn't, yet.

At 21, Benson is playing 20:13 a night (up from 15:53) and is on the ice for 72% of Buffalo's power-play chances. The Sabres get 57% of the 5v5 expected goals (chance quality) with him out there, 11 points better than without him, and Evolving-Hockey had him in the 98th percentile among forwards for driving chances last season. He sets the table: 14 assists, and Matthew Fairburn's post Tuesday had him finding Tage Thompson in the slot.

But he has two goals on 8.2 expected, shooting 3.9% against a talent range near 11%. That's the biggest gap between chances and goals on the team, and it's why he ranks near the bottom of the league in wins added from goals while being one of Buffalo's best players. In a team video headline he put it simply: "We Have To Bear Down, But Just Got To Stick With It." The Sabres have gone five without a win. His finishing is the most fixable thing on that list.
headline: Benson has arrived, except for the goals
